message.content: {"note_claim": "The House of Commons Library says the claims that owning a domestic property used for prayer exempts council tax have no basis in council tax law, and it is not possible to avoid council tax by claiming religious use.", "label": "SUPPORTS", "quote": "These claims have no basis in council tax law. It is not possible for owners of domestic property to avoid council tax by claiming that their property, or part of it, is used for religious purposes.", "reason": "The Full Fact page contains the exact House of Commons Library quote used in the note and rates the prayer-room council tax exemption claim as false."}

parsed.note_claim: The House of Commons Library says the claims that owning a domestic property used for prayer exempts council tax have no basis in council tax law, and it is not possible to avoid council tax by claiming religious use.
parsed.label: SUPPORTS
parsed.quote: These claims have no basis in council tax law. It is not possible for owners of domestic property to avoid council tax by claiming that their property, or part of it, is used for religious purposes.
parsed.reason: The Full Fact page contains the exact House of Commons Library quote used in the note and rates the prayer-room council tax exemption claim as false.
